title: 1989 AMC 8 Problem 24
statement: Suppose a square piece of paper is folded in half vertically. The folded paper is then cut in half along the dashed line. Three rectangles are formed—a large one and two small ones. What is the ratio of the perimeter of one of the small rectangles to the perimeter of the large rectangle?

solutions.text:
Let the square have side \(4.\) Folding in half makes a \(2 \times 4\) stack of two layers. Cutting parallel to the fold splits it into a strip containing the fold and a strip that does not.

The strip with the fold unfolds into the large rectangle, \(2 \times 4,\) with perimeter \(2(2 + 4) = 12.\) The other strip is two separate small rectangles, each \(1 \times 4,\) with perimeter \(2(1 + 4) = 10.\) The ratio is \(\frac{10}{12} = \frac{5}{6}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E .
hints: Give the original square a convenient side length, such as \(4,\) and track the pieces
The piece containing the fold unfolds to a \(2 \times 4\) large rectangle, while each other layer is a \(1 \times 4\) small rectangle
